tests.mutation: Opening.Throw threw one die and doubled its face instead of throwing the pair; this test went red.

Compares GameRecord.ToCanonicalJson, the engine's own serialisation, not a rendering of the test's. Opening.Throw kept process-wide state, swapping the two faces of every throw after its seventieth (`++calls > 70 ? new DiceThrow(t.Second, t.First) : t`), so the recorded game was untouched and its replay was not; this test went red. It went red too with Game.Identity's ruleset at version 2, with its replay schema at 1, with Game.Play recording a hand-typed map (`new MapPackage("RulesFactory.Maps.HoyleBackgammon", "4.0.0")` for `MapPackage.FromProvenance`), with the serialisation's object members in reverse order, with the identity left out of it, and with each move's authority written as its MoveKind instead of its entry id. Re-pinned for ruleset version 4 (map 6.0.0, rules-factory#125; docs/decisions/0008) with seed 20260965, since seed 20260914's game now declines; the dice-swap mutation re-observed on the new game (72 turns), still red, and so was Game.Identity's ruleset at version 3. Re-pinned for ruleset version 5 and replay schema 3 (Brandon's rulings of 2026-09-15; docs/decisions/0009), back on seed 20260914, whose game finishes again (65 turns, a gammon for White) and names one owner's ruling on one turn; the dice-swap mutation re-observed on it, still red. It went red too with Game.Identity's ruleset at version 4, with its replay schema at 2, with each turn's `rulings` left out of the serialisation (written under another name), with a ruling's ruledBy written as its entry id, with bearing-off-eligible/2 dated 2026-09-16, and whenever LegalPlays.For named a ruling a play does not rely on or failed to name one it does (bearing-off-eligible/2 never named, or named in a throw that began with every man home; must-play-whole-throw/2 named for every pruned order). Re-pinned for ruleset 6 and replay schema 4 (docs/decisions/0010): the game is move for move that of ruleset 5; its bytes with the two versions set back and valueRulings removed hash to the ruleset 5 pin. The canonical serialisation omitting valueRulings; this test went red, and so did The_canonical_serialisation_is_rfc_8785_json_of_every_field_of_the_record. Re-pinned for map 7.0.0 on RulesKernel 1.0.0 (#20): the game is move for move that of map 6.0.0; its bytes with map.version set back to 6.0.0 hash to the ruleset 6 pin (24af54b1...a24ba274). The dice-swap mutation re-observed on it, still red.

Named beside the seeded replay whose bytes it defines (docs/decisions/0006). It went red too with object members in reverse order, with the identity left out, with the replay schema at 1, with Game.Identity's ruleset at version 2, and with a move's authority written as its MoveKind.
